content:
Currently, DerivingHandler has the type:

Array Name → CommandElabM Bool

I think this type permits more than is necessary, for the following reasons.

  1. Array Name is the array of declaration names supplied to the deriving command. However, deriving type class instances should be performed independently for each declaration. Therefore, DerivingHandler should only need to take a single Name.
  2. The use of CommandElabM makes the handler’s responsibilities unclear. A deriving handler should take a declaration name decl and generate the syntax for an instance command for decl. If so, the following return type should be sufficient:
TermElabM (Option (TSyntax `command))

Benefits of This Proposal

  • By accepting a Name rather than an Array Name, the optimization of processing multiple declarations in parallel could be implemented centrally.
    With the current Array Name argument, the decision of whether and how to process multiple declarations in parallel is left to each individual DerivingHandler implementation.

  • One advantage of returning syntax objects is that it separates code generation from execution. I think this may make testing and debugging easier, but I am not very confident about this, so I would welcome counterarguments.
what if it doesn't produce a syntax, but instead runs some command?

@Aaron Liu

If there are cases like that, then changing it to TermElabM certainly would not make sense.

Are there actually any such cases?
I don't know any deriving handlers, but it certainly seems plausible given the return type

In my opinion, deriving handlers shouldn't use command syntax at all! Using syntax makes everything more error prone and slower. But, of course, it's harder to write a deriving handler that just generates the instance using meta code. What I mean by more error prone is this btw:

structure Test (α : {_n : Nat} → Bool) where
  val : Nat
deriving BEq -- error! don't know how to synthesize implicit argument `_n`

Like, you'd expect that to work, right? Even if the signature is kinda odd, that seems like something the deriving handler should support; and yet, it just gives me an obscure error message. If you want to write a syntax-based deriving handler properly, there are so many things to keep in mind that are easy to forget. Using meta code directly is generally more robust (if done well).

So, changing CommandElabM Bool to TermElabM (Option (TSyntax `command)) would make things worse, in my opinion.

Also, you're right that most deriving handlers just iterate the list of declaration names (except ToExpr which behaves incorrectly) but that is really a waste when deriving instances for a mutual inductive. This simple piece of code generates 9 declarations of the shape α → α → Bool (three for each type) where just three would've been sufficient:

mutual

inductive A where
  | base
  | foo (x : B)

inductive B where
  | base
  | bar (x : C)

inductive C where
  | base
  | baz (x : A)

end

deriving instance BEq for A, B, C

In general, I think much is wrong with how deriving handlers are written in core and I would like a refactor but restricting the type of DerivingHandler would certainly be step back. We should use the flexibility we're given!
Robin, thanks. I hadn’t considered types defined using mutual. I learned a lot from your explanation.
